_comment: Release state per kernel and level (decision D14). `release` entries must stay within `_limits.release` times the instructions per sample of the comparison, `dev` entries within `_limits.dev`; `goal` marks the entries at or below it in the results. `info` entries are reported and never judged; their `waiver` text says why the comparison is not fair. A `waiver` on a `release` or `dev` entry names the open item in docs/open-items.md that tracks a limit that is not met yet; it never hides the numbers. The level `avx2-runtime` is judged against our own `avx2` numbers with `_limits.runtime`; entries for it are needed only to relax that. A `cycle_waiver` on a SIMD entry and level exempts it from the gate of D321 (`cargo xtask check cycles`: in the simulated cycle tables of docs/performance.md the entry must not be slower than its `_fallback` entry on the reference model or the counter-model); its text gives the reason and names the open item in docs/open-items.md, and the check fails on a waiver whose gap is closed. See docs/performance.md.

sse2.accuracy_waiver: 133.3 dB against 134.3 dB for CMSIS-DSP's `arm_fir_decimate_f32` on the count input (SNR against the f64 model): the same accuracy class in another summation order. Both sum each output in one `f32` accumulator without FMA (CMSIS-DSP is built with `-ffp-contract=off`); CMSIS-DSP adds the products from the oldest sample on (taps descending in SDRk's order), ours in ascending tap order, which the numeric contract of the `C32` fallback fixes (docs/kernels.md). The difference is the rounding of the other order on this input; the grouped fallback has the bits of the one-at-a-time sum (unit tests), so the fallback before it had the same 133.3 dB; the f64 golden vectors give 143.3 dB (`m10_n63`, optimum 152.1 dB) and 144.3 dB (`m3_n31`, optimum 151.9 dB)

sse2.waiver: 1.36 times the instructions of CMSIS-DSP's `arm_fir_decimate_q15` at this level, within the `dev` limit. The gap is not the accuracy class: CMSIS-DSP sums in `q63_t` as we do (exact 64-bit sums, one saturation per output; it truncates with `>> 15` where we round, one add per output), so it is our code generation. CMSIS-DSP's tap loop per output is a reduction that the C compiler vectorizes (`pmullw`/`pmulhw`, widening to 64 bits, `paddq`); our outputs, whose windows lie `M` samples apart (one slice per output, 16 `i64` accumulators per group), compile to scalar 64-bit multiply-adds. Inlining the per-tap step of the group (an out-of-line closure before, one call per tap) took it from 178.89 to 118.11 instructions per sample. the gap in simulated cycles is tracked in issue #134: a vectorizable `Q15` form of the strided group
